subject: Computer Networking
title: Smart City Networks
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Smart City Networks.

hook.text: Traffic lights that adapt to congestion. Air sensors that trigger alerts. Smart cities run on data.

buildup.text: Smart city platforms collect from thousands of sensors: traffic, air quality, noise, energy, water.

discovery.text: 5G slicing gives each city service its own virtual network. Emergencies get guaranteed bandwidth.

twist.text: Privacy is the biggest worry. Cameras and sensors blur the line between smart and surveilled.

climax.text: Barcelona, Singapore, and Helsinki lead smart city efforts. They show both promise and pitfalls.

punchline.text: Smart cities connect everything. The challenge: keeping privacy.

quiz.question: What does network slicing enable for smart cities?
options: Dedicated virtual networks for different services with guaranteed resources
Faster Wi-Fi for residents in their homes
Cheaper internet subscriptions for city residents

details.summary: Smart city networks connect thousands of sensors, cameras, traffic lights, and utilities across urban areas to optimize services and reduce costs. They combine fiber backbone, cellular, LPWAN, and mesh technologies to create a unified infrastructure that enables data-driven urban management.
details.whyItMatters: Cities consume 75 percent of global energy and house most of the population. Smart networking makes cities more efficient, sustainable, and responsive to citizen needs through real-time data.
takeaways: Multiple network technologies create a unified urban infrastructure
Real-time data optimizes traffic, energy, and public services
Privacy and security challenges scale with the sensor network

faq.question: What network technologies do smart cities use?
faq.answer: Fiber connects major infrastructure. Cellular and 5G serve mobile devices and cameras. LoRaWAN and NB-IoT connect thousands of low-power sensors for parking, waste, and environmental monitoring. Wi-Fi provides public connectivity. Mesh networks extend coverage in dense urban areas.

faq.question: What are the privacy concerns with smart cities?
faq.answer: Pervasive sensors and cameras can track citizen movements and behavior. Centralized data creates high-value targets for attackers.
